closest_functional_analogue.name: flying fishes
closest_functional_analogue.function: glides over water after leaving it
closest_functional_analogue.function_operational_definition: leaves the water and travels through air over a measurable distance without flapping-powered thrust. Satisfied by a taxon for which a glide distance or duration is reported, or for which the gliding habit is the taxon-defining behaviour in the primary literature.
closest_functional_analogue.function_signal: INFERRED, not specified: no desired-phenotype text reached this module, so the function was taken from the design's identity (zebrafish-adult). A different desired phenotype would change the requirement set and so the whole ledger.
closest_functional_analogue.basis: satisfies the operational definition of "glides over water after leaving it"
closest_functional_analogue.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json); Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: Exocoetidae are the gliding clade of the Beloniformes; Daane 2021 groups the family as the gliding end of a four-group series (needlefish -> halfbeak -> gliding halfbeak -> flying fish) and measures the fin proportion that supports the glide
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json)

evidence.claim: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.687 (range 0.406-0.823, n = 49 museum specimens)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

phylogenetic.mrca_source: Ensembl Compara orthologue records fetched for the requirement loci (homology taxonomy_level); see C:/Temp/functional-cache/ortho/
phylogenetic.dated_divergence_note: NOT asserted: no source fetched in this thread dates the Otophysi-Acanthomorpha split, so no number is given rather than a remembered one

functional.why_unmeasurable: The design side has no number. design-validation/REPORT.md axis 1 is CANNOT SCORE on BOTH sides at once: no fetched source gives an adult zebrafish pectoral fin length / SL (development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs returns finLength_SL: null), and the winged zebrafish's own value exists only inside Daane 2021 Figure 4B, which this project refuses to digitise. The single number that would settle the headline question is unavailable at both ends.

distance.rule: the two distances are reported separately and never combined: a close functional analogue may be phylogenetically remote, and that is the whole point of choosing by function

evidence.claim: an independent, shallower glider inside the same order: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.274 (range 0.175-0.388, n = 19)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: gliding halfbeaks carry about as many of the Exocoetidae-derived coding states as flying fishes do, at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not scale with fin length
evidence.source: sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] (our own re-read of Daane sheet G per species from the captured exons)

closest_functional_analogue.data_poor_statement: The ONLY analogue for this function has a genome and nothing else: no transcriptome, no proteome, no expression atlas, no mutant, no functional assay, and 9 of 3,860 genes carry an identifier for it. Every functional requirement derived from it is therefore derived from SEQUENCE and from the curated comparative analysis in one paper - never from a measurement of the analogue doing the thing.

functional_data_we_hold.genome: a draft genome and gene set exist for ONE flying fish, Hirundichthys speculiger (Xu et al. 2021, Front Genet 12:695700, doi 10.3389/fgene.2021.695700, assembly GCA_018398805.1)
functional_data_we_hold.transcriptome: NONE. omics/transcriptomic/SOURCES.md: no flying-fish RNA-seq, raw or processed, exists in SRA/ENA/GEO/ArrayExpress; 3,485 loose Europe PMC hits and not one flying-fish transcriptome. In particular NO pectoral-fin expression data
functional_data_we_hold.proteome: NONE. omics/proteomic/SOURCES.md: 3 UniProt rows for flying-fish entries in 199,149; no MS evidence, no abundance, no structures
functional_data_we_hold.focal_gene_ids: omics/genes.json coverage.flying_fish = 9 of 3,860 genes carry a Hirundichthys identifier; 7 of 9 are clean reciprocal best hits (genotype/sequence-layer.json counts)
functional_data_we_hold.mutants_or_assays: NONE. No flying fish has ever been mutated, knocked down or functionally assayed in any source we fetched

closest_functional_analogue.direction_detected_by: the base does not satisfy the function and the design is to gain it

direction_evidence.claim: no glide, leap or aerial behaviour is reported for Danio rerio in any source this project fetched, and its pectoral fin length / SL is NOT MEASURED IN ANY FETCHED SOURCE (genotype/compare-2x2.json panel A). So "the base lacks the function" rests on the absence of any report, which is weaker than a measurement and is labelled as such
direction_evidence.source: genotype/compare-2x2.json; sim-engine organism document zebrafish-adult (pectoral_len_over_SL kind "assumed")

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution

coverage.note: we can assess 22 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

functional_resolution.gate: FAIL: 19 difference(s) from the closest functional analogue are UNRESOLVED; the design is not functionally accounted for, whatever the similarity scores
functional_resolution.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout). A functional-analogue ledger, not a validity claim. It says how each difference between the design and its closest FUNCTIONAL analogue is accounted for, and what the evidence for that account is. A COMPENSATORY entry is a hypothesis about an unobserved mechanism and is reported apart from demonstrated resolutions; it is never counted as one.
functional_resolution.source: sim-engine/validate/functional/ (built by another thread; consumed through validate/functional-interface.mjs)

target_function.why: no flight intent is declared, so the function taken as desired is the one every fish here has: hold station in a current
target_function.inferred_from: zebrafish-adult | the repository's own zebrafish-adult, unedited | zebrafish-adult | zebrafish (Danio rerio), adult
target_function.statement: NO SPEC WAS GIVEN, so the target function was INFERRED from the design's declared intent (no flight intent is declared, so the function taken as desired is the one every fish here has: hold station in a current). It is what we chose to test, not what we were asked for. Pass opts.spec to test the real requirement.

criteria.source_text: inferred: hold station at 0.2 m/s, the current scenario's own default test speed

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 180 d after hatching (182 dpf), SL 38.83 mm, Adult

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: Ucrit(T, age) = k(age) x SL x r(T); k = 15.5 SL/s for >= 28 dpf (Plaut 2000), 10.5 SL/s at 14 dpf (Umax 12.1 / 1.15), linear between; 0.03 m/s at 5 dpf, linear to 14 dpf

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution

coverage.note: we can assess 0 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

functional_resolution.gate: no differences were classified: the ledger is empty, which is not evidence that there are none
functional_resolution.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout). A functional-analogue ledger, not a validity claim. It says how each difference between the design and its closest FUNCTIONAL analogue is accounted for, and what the evidence for that account is. A COMPENSATORY entry is a hypothesis about an unobserved mechanism and is reported apart from demonstrated resolutions; it is never counted as one.
functional_resolution.source: sim-engine/validate/functional/ (built by another thread; consumed through validate/functional-interface.mjs)

target_function.why: the design's declared intent is a gliding fish
target_function.inferred_from: winged-zebrafish-with-genotype | repository winged-zebrafish design plus the two loci of the Daane 2021 double heterozygote (sequences/engineered-diff.json) | winged-zebrafish | winged zebrafish - zebrafish with the pectoral fin proportion moved toward the flying fish | lat4a nr21 (Daane 2021), heterozygous | kcnh2a lof dt2 inversion (Daane 2021), heterozygous; 0 amino acids
target_function.statement: NO SPEC WAS GIVEN, so the target function was INFERRED from the design's declared intent (the design's declared intent is a gliding fish). It is what we chose to test, not what we were asked for. Pass opts.spec to test the real requirement.

criteria.source_text: inferred: a realistic glide. 10 m from a 1 m launch, inside the 5-75 m band the independent harness scores the real flying fish against (STUDIO-RESULTS W9: 36.5 m at 15 m/s, pass-rests-on-assumed)

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 180 d after hatching (182 dpf), SL 38.83 mm, Adult
per_stage.limiting_factor: cannot glide: the reachable launch speed 0.67 m/s is below v_min 8.64 m/s, so lift cannot carry the weight [achieved in 0.0 % of 200 draws over the stated input distributions; median 0 m, 5-95 % 0 to 0]
per_stage.out_of_validity: Mass 0.0006943 kg is outside 0.02-0.4 kg (polar specimens 0.04-0.06 kg; field fliers to ~0.4 kg): polar extrapolated. Mean-chord Reynolds number ~3.1e+3 is outside 5e3-1e5 around the polar's Re ~1e4 (Park & Choi: 'gliding flying fish (Re ~10^4)'; air kinematic viscosity 1.46e-5 m2/s). glide_range_total_m exceeds the Lean bound whenever the kinetic phase is non-zero; only glide_range_lean_bound_m is covered by glide_range_le. Fick bound: arterial PO2 taken equal to air PO2 and gills taken to work in air; gills do not ventilate in air (physiology chain), so for a gill-breather this is a generous upper bound. TFF: NOTES-FOR-HUB.md item 2 says only 29.5% of the flight muscle the simulator charges fits in the body. This module uses no muscle power (the Fick bound is the cap), so the issue does not enter here; any muscle-based claim for the TFF must take it into account.

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

causal_chain.weakest_link: molecular_function->process, which is empty of experiment. The transport function is solid but entirely from mammalian orthologs read as abstracts, and nothing bridges 'moves leucine/methionine' to 'changes fin ray length'. A second, nearly as bad break: all six ZFIN rows and every phenotype statement come from one publication (ZDB-PUB-210918-31 / PMID 34534441), so this gene has no independent replication.
gaps: No pathway or process step for Lat4a in the fin: no mTOR/mTORC1 readout, no amino acid measurement in fin tissue, no substrate rescue, no transcriptional target.
Zebrafish Lat4a transport activity has never been measured; the molecular function is imported from human/mouse orthologs.
No cell type resolved for lat4a in the fin (no transplantation, no clonal mosaic, no cell-type driver).
Direction of the T200K effect on transport is unknown: the allele is a genetic gain of function but no transport assay was done on it, so whether it moves more or less amino acid is undetermined.
Every fin phenotype and every ZFIN row for this gene traces to a single paper (PMID 34534441); no independent replication was found.
Flying-fish Lat4a (F326L) was never functionally tested in any species; it is a convergent substitution in a sequence alignment.

closest_functional_analogue.function_operational_definition: level or climbing flight produced by flapping, sustained beyond a ballistic or gliding trajectory, with an aerobic power supply

closest_functional_analogue.basis: NO ORGANISM WE MAY READ SATISFIES "sustained powered (flapping) flight". The nearest partial analogues are bats (supplies: powered flapping flight itself, with an aerobic power supply, in an animal whose sequences we may read); flying fishes (supplies: the airborne half: a teleost that leaves the water and travels through air, with the enlarged pectoral fin that makes it possible, and a sequenced genome) - each named with what it does NOT supply, so neither is mistaken for the analogue. The closest RELATIVE is not offered in its place: relatedness is not function, which is the whole premise of this module.

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution

functional_resolution.gate: no differences were classified: the ledger is empty, which is not evidence that there are none
functional_resolution.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout). A functional-analogue ledger, not a validity claim. It says how each difference between the design and its closest FUNCTIONAL analogue is accounted for, and what the evidence for that account is. A COMPENSATORY entry is a hypothesis about an unobserved mechanism and is reported apart from demonstrated resolutions; it is never counted as one.

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band applies to this animal at this stage

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 365 d after hatching, SL 206.2 mm

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band applies to this animal at this stage

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)

Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; feasible (hold station) = current <= Ucrit; survives = null

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

closest_functional_analogue.function_operational_definition: leaves the water and travels through air over a measurable distance without flapping-powered thrust. Satisfied by a taxon for which a glide distance or duration is reported, or for which the gliding habit is the taxon-defining behaviour in the primary literature.
closest_functional_analogue.function_signal: INFERRED, not specified: no desired-phenotype text reached this module, so the function was taken from the design's identity (ff-zf-chimera). A different desired phenotype would change the requirement set and so the whole ledger.
closest_functional_analogue.basis: satisfies the operational definition of "glides over water after leaving it"
closest_functional_analogue.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json); Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: Exocoetidae are the gliding clade of the Beloniformes; Daane 2021 groups the family as the gliding end of a four-group series (needlefish -> halfbeak -> gliding halfbeak -> flying fish) and measures the fin proportion that supports the glide
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A (genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json)

evidence.claim: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.687 (range 0.406-0.823, n = 49 museum specimens)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

phylogenetic.dated_divergence_note: NOT asserted: no source fetched in this thread dates the Otophysi-Acanthomorpha split, so no number is given rather than a remembered one

functional.why_unmeasurable: The design side has no number. design-validation/REPORT.md axis 1 is CANNOT SCORE on BOTH sides at once: no fetched source gives an adult zebrafish pectoral fin length / SL (development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs returns finLength_SL: null), and the winged zebrafish's own value exists only inside Daane 2021 Figure 4B, which this project refuses to digitise. The single number that would settle the headline question is unavailable at both ends.

distance.rule: the two distances are reported separately and never combined: a close functional analogue may be phylogenetically remote, and that is the whole point of choosing by function

evidence.claim: an independent, shallower glider inside the same order: pectoral fin length / SL median 0.274 (range 0.175-0.388, n = 19)
evidence.source: Daane et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441, Data S1 sheet A

evidence.claim: gliding halfbeaks carry about as many of the Exocoetidae-derived coding states as flying fishes do, at a fin ratio 2.5x smaller, so derived-state count does not scale with fin length
evidence.source: sequences/progression.json read_this_first[1] (our own re-read of Daane sheet G per species from the captured exons)

closest_functional_analogue.data_poor_statement: The ONLY analogue for this function has a genome and nothing else: no transcriptome, no proteome, no expression atlas, no mutant, no functional assay, and 9 of 3,860 genes carry an identifier for it. Every functional requirement derived from it is therefore derived from SEQUENCE and from the curated comparative analysis in one paper - never from a measurement of the analogue doing the thing.

functional_data_we_hold.genome: a draft genome and gene set exist for ONE flying fish, Hirundichthys speculiger (Xu et al. 2021, Front Genet 12:695700, doi 10.3389/fgene.2021.695700, assembly GCA_018398805.1)
functional_data_we_hold.transcriptome: NONE. omics/transcriptomic/SOURCES.md: no flying-fish RNA-seq, raw or processed, exists in SRA/ENA/GEO/ArrayExpress; 3,485 loose Europe PMC hits and not one flying-fish transcriptome. In particular NO pectoral-fin expression data
functional_data_we_hold.proteome: NONE. omics/proteomic/SOURCES.md: 3 UniProt rows for flying-fish entries in 199,149; no MS evidence, no abundance, no structures
functional_data_we_hold.focal_gene_ids: omics/genes.json coverage.flying_fish = 9 of 3,860 genes carry a Hirundichthys identifier; 7 of 9 are clean reciprocal best hits (genotype/sequence-layer.json counts)
functional_data_we_hold.mutants_or_assays: NONE. No flying fish has ever been mutated, knocked down or functionally assayed in any source we fetched

closest_functional_analogue.direction_detected_by: the base already satisfies the function and nothing in the request removes it, so the design is read as keeping or extending it

direction_evidence.claim: the base (Hirundichthys / Exocoetidae) already satisfies "glides over water after leaving it"

resolution.note: demonstrated and hypothesised are never summed; "could be compensated" is not a resolution

coverage.note: we can assess 0 of 73 requirements; the rest are unassessable, each with its own stated reason. ZERO of the loci have flying-fish expression or functional-assay data of any kind, because no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or assay exists in any archive we searched. Every "requirement" is therefore a SEQUENCE STATE in the analogue, never a measured function of the analogue.

functional_resolution.gate: no differences were classified: the ledger is empty, which is not evidence that there are none
functional_resolution.scope: A functional-analogue ledger for ONE function, built from the loci one paper reports as known to differ in the analogue. Every requirement is a SEQUENCE STATE of the analogue, never a measured function of it: no flying-fish transcriptome, proteome, mutant or functional assay exists in any archive we searched, so nothing here says what the analogue's genes DO. Resolutions above UNRESOLVED carry their evidence and its kind; hypothesised and demonstrated resolutions are reported as two numbers and are never added together. No Aves data (frozen holdout). A functional-analogue ledger, not a validity claim. It says how each difference between the design and its closest FUNCTIONAL analogue is accounted for, and what the evidence for that account is. A COMPENSATORY entry is a hypothesis about an unobserved mechanism and is reported apart from demonstrated resolutions; it is never counted as one.

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 365 d after hatching, SL 206.2 mm
per_stage.limiting_factor: blended species: no measured leap or burst speed exists for a blend, and none is invented

species_gate.note: the species matches the flier gate but the STAGE does not: the 15-20 m/s taxi band is measured for ADULT flying fish only; the engine's own launch speed for this STATE is not sourced (scenarios/glide.mjs organismLaunchSpeed), so no launch-speed spread is drawn and none is invented. The spread below comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)
